chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Abdullah al-Razi narrated to me from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan ibn Sadaqah, who said:
Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) said: 'Take a nap (qaylulah), for indeed Allah provides food and water to the fasting person in his sleep.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلُ: Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (Imam Musa al-Kadhim, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of taking a midday nap while fasting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) highlights the spiritual and physical benefits of the midday nap (*qaylulah*) for fasting individuals, noting that Allah provides sustenance in their sleep. This tradition underscores the holistic nature of fasting in Shia jurisprudence, where rest is not merely a physical necessity but a divinely rewarded act that alleviates the hardship of abstinence. The mention of 'eating and drinking in sleep' serves as a metaphor for the soul's refreshment and the tangible reward awaiting the believer.
